lines.text: Shuffle eight kids into a line. Will two of the girls end up side by side?
lines.caption: Shuffle eight kids into a line. Will two of the girls end up side by side?

lines.text: Here's a surprise. <short pause> More often than not, they do!
lines.caption: Here's a surprise. More often than not, they do!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the exact chance, together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the exact chance, together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Five boys and three girls stand in a row, in a random order. Every order is equally likely.
lines.caption: Five boys and three girls stand in a row, in a random order. Every order is equally likely.

lines.text: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?
lines.caption: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's picture eight spots in a row, numbered one to eight.
lines.caption: Let's picture eight spots in a row, numbered one to eight.

lines.text: This line is good. There's at least one boy between any two girls.
lines.caption: This line is good. There's at least one boy between any two girls.

lines.text: This line is bad. Two girls are standing side by side.
lines.caption: This line is bad. Two girls are standing side by side.

lines.text: So we want the fraction of all the lines that are good.
lines.caption: So we want the fraction of all the lines that are good.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's a trick. We only care WHERE the girls stand.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's a trick. We only care WHERE the girls stand.

lines.text: Say the girls take spots one, four, and seven.
lines.caption: Say the girls take spots one, four, and seven.

lines.text: The girls can fill those spots in three, times two, times one. That's six orders.
lines.caption: The girls can fill those spots in three, times two, times one. That's six orders.

lines.text: The boys fill the other five spots in five, times four, times three, times two, times one.
lines.caption: The boys fill the other five spots in five, times four, times three, times two, times one.

lines.text: That's one hundred twenty orders.
lines.caption: That's one hundred twenty orders.

lines.text: Six times one hundred twenty is seven hundred twenty. It's the same for EVERY three spots!
lines.caption: Six times one hundred twenty is seven hundred twenty. It's the same for EVERY three spots!

lines.text: So each set of three spots is equally likely. We can count spots, not names.
lines.caption: So each set of three spots is equally likely. We can count spots, not names.

lines.text: How many ways can we pick three spots out of eight?
lines.caption: How many ways can we pick three spots out of eight?

lines.text: Pick one spot, then another, then another. Eight, times seven, times six.
lines.caption: Pick one spot, then another, then another. Eight, times seven, times six.

lines.text: That's three hundred thirty-six. But each set of spots got picked in six different orders.
lines.caption: That's three hundred thirty-six. But each set of spots got picked in six different orders.

lines.text: So divide by six. There are fifty-six sets of spots in all.
lines.caption: So divide by six. There are fifty-six sets of spots in all.

lines.text: Now let's list the good sets, sorted by where the first girl stands.
lines.caption: Now let's list the good sets, sorted by where the first girl stands.

lines.text: First girl in spot one. The second girl skips spot two, so she can stand in three.
lines.caption: First girl in spot one. The second girl skips spot two, so she can stand in three.

lines.text: Then the last girl skips four. She has four choices: five, six, seven, or eight.
lines.caption: Then the last girl skips four. She has four choices: five, six, seven, or eight.

lines.text: Move the second girl to four, then five, then six. That's three choices, then two, then one.
lines.caption: Move the second girl to four, then five, then six. That's three choices, then two, then one.

lines.text: Four, plus three, plus two, plus one. Ten good sets start in spot one.
lines.caption: Four, plus three, plus two, plus one. Ten good sets start in spot one.

lines.text: Start in spot two: three, plus two, plus one. That's six sets.
lines.caption: Start in spot two: three, plus two, plus one. That's six sets.

lines.text: Spot three gives two plus one, three sets. Spot four gives just one: four, six, eight.
lines.caption: Spot three gives two plus one, three sets. Spot four gives just one: four, six, eight.

lines.text: Ten, plus six, plus three, plus one. That's twenty good sets!
lines.caption: Ten, plus six, plus three, plus one. That's twenty good sets!

lines.text: Twenty over fifty-six. Divide both by four. That's five over fourteen. <short pause> Choice C!
lines.caption: Twenty over fifty-six. Divide both by four. That's five over fourteen. Choice C!

lines.text: Here's a faster way. Line up the five boys first.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way. Line up the five boys first.

lines.text: Look at the gaps: four between the boys, plus one at each end. That's six gaps.
lines.caption: Look at the gaps: four between the boys, plus one at each end. That's six gaps.

lines.text: Two girls in the same gap would touch. So each gap gets at most one girl.
lines.caption: Two girls in the same gap would touch. So each gap gets at most one girl.

lines.text: We choose three of the six gaps. Six, times five, times four, over six, like before.
lines.caption: We choose three of the six gaps. Six, times five, times four, over six, like before.

lines.text: That's twenty again! Twenty over fifty-six is five over fourteen. And we never needed a list.
lines.caption: That's twenty again! Twenty over fifty-six is five over fourteen. And we never needed a list.

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When the line is long, and a list would take forever.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When the line is long, and a list would take forever.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice B uses only five gaps. Three of five gaps is ten ways. Ten over fifty-six.
lines.caption: Choice B uses only five gaps. Three of five gaps is ten ways. Ten over fifty-six.

lines.text: That's five over twenty-eight. We forgot the gap at one end!
lines.caption: That's five over twenty-eight. We forgot the gap at one end!

lines.text: Choice A is what you'd get with no end gaps. Three of four gaps is four ways.
lines.caption: Choice A is what you'd get with no end gaps. Three of four gaps is four ways.

lines.text: Four over fifty-six is one over fourteen. But a girl CAN stand at either end!
lines.caption: Four over fifty-six is one over fourteen. But a girl CAN stand at either end!

lines.text: Choice D is what you'd get from three girls over eight kids. It ignores touching.
lines.caption: Choice D is what you'd get from three girls over eight kids. It ignores touching.

lines.text: Choice E is what you'd get if touching and not touching were equally likely.
lines.caption: Choice E is what you'd get if touching and not touching were equally likely.

lines.text: They're not! Twenty sets are good, and thirty-six are bad.
lines.caption: They're not! Twenty sets are good, and thirty-six are bad.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. When you count gaps, always check both ends.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. When you count gaps, always check both ends.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now there are four boys and three girls.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now there are four boys and three girls.

lines.text: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?
lines.caption: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Four boys make three gaps between them, plus two ends. Five gaps.
lines.caption: Let's check. Four boys make three gaps between them, plus two ends. Five gaps.

lines.text: Choose three of the five gaps. Five, times four, times three, over six. That's ten.
lines.caption: Choose three of the five gaps. Five, times four, times three, over six. That's ten.

lines.text: Now all the sets of spots. Seven, times six, times five, over six. That's thirty-five.
lines.caption: Now all the sets of spots. Seven, times six, times five, over six. That's thirty-five.

lines.text: Ten over thirty-five. Divide both by five. That's two over seven! Amazing work if you got it!
lines.caption: Ten over thirty-five. Divide both by five. That's two over seven! Amazing work if you got it!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Only the spots of the girls matter, and every set of spots is equally likely.
lines.caption: Only the spots of the girls matter, and every set of spots is equally likely.

lines.text: To keep the girls apart, place the boys first. Then choose gaps, one girl each, counting both ends.
lines.caption: To keep the girls apart, place the boys first. Then choose gaps, one girl each, counting both ends.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
